learn.title: Relational data: choosing the right SQL and open-source database service
objectives: Choose between Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance and SQL Server on Azure VMs from feature, compatibility and control requirements
Identify instance-level features (SQL Server Agent, cross-database queries, CLR, Service Broker, Database Mail, linked servers) that rule out Azure SQL Database
Recognise features that neither PaaS option supports (FILESTREAM, SSAS, SSRS as a service, extended stored procedures, xp_cmdshell, OS access) and route them to SQL Server on Azure VMs
Recommend Azure Database for PostgreSQL or MySQL flexible server for open-source engines, and know which older services are retired
Reduce licensing and management cost with Azure Hybrid Benefit, the SQL IaaS Agent extension and free editions where they fit
concepts: Azure SQL Database
Fully managed PaaS database scoped to one database (single database or elastic pool). Lowest admin effort, but no instance-level features such as SQL Server Agent, CLR or cross-database queries.
Logical server
The container for SQL Database logins, firewall rules and Microsoft Entra admin. It is not a SQL Server instance and its databases don't share compute unless they are in an elastic pool.
Elastic pool
A set of SQL databases that share one pool of resources. A good fit for many small databases whose peaks happen at different times.
Azure SQL Managed Instance

PaaS SQL Server instance injected into your VNet with near 100% engine compatibility: SQL Agent, cross-database queries, CLR (from binary), Service Broker, Database Mail, linked servers to SQL Server and native RESTORE FROM URL.
SQL Server on Azure VMs

IaaS. You get full control of the OS and SQL Server, any version or edition, and features PaaS can't run (FILESTREAM, SSAS, SSRS, xp_cmdshell, third-party agents). You also own patching and configuration.
SQL IaaS Agent extension
Free extension for SQL Server VMs. It unlocks portal management, licence-type switching, automated backup, automated patching and Key Vault integration.
Azure Hybrid Benefit

Use SQL Server licences with Software Assurance (or qualifying subscriptions) to pay a lower base rate. For SQL Database it applies only to vCore provisioned compute, not DTU or serverless. Enterprise: 1 core = 4 General Purpose vCores.
Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server
Managed community PostgreSQL with stop/start, Burstable to Memory Optimized compute, built-in PgBouncer and allow-listed extensions such as PostGIS. Elastic clusters add Citus-based scale-out.
Azure Database for MySQL flexible server
Managed community MySQL. Single Server is retired, and Azure Database for MariaDB is also retired, so MariaDB workloads move here.
MI update policy
Sets which SQL Server engine version the instance matches. The SQL Server 2022 or 2025 policies keep native backups restorable to that SQL Server version. Always-up-to-date gives the newest features.
Elastic jobs
The SQL Database replacement for SQL Server Agent jobs. Runs T-SQL on a schedule across many databases.
Azure SQL Edge
IoT edge SQL engine. It retired on 30 September 2025, so don't recommend it for new designs.
comparisons: SQL Database vs SQL Managed Instance

Pick SQL Database when the app uses one database and no instance features. Pick Managed Instance when it needs SQL Agent, cross-database queries, CLR, Service Broker, Database Mail, linked servers or native .bak restore.
Managed Instance vs SQL Server on Azure VM

Managed Instance keeps PaaS benefits when compatibility is enough. Move to a VM when you need OS access, FILESTREAM/FileTable, SSAS/SSRS on the same host, xp_cmdshell, unsupported trace flags, a specific older version, or control over patch timing.
PostgreSQL flexible server vs PostgreSQL on a VM
Flexible server is managed and supports allow-listed extensions. Use a VM only when you need superuser/OS access or an extension the service doesn't support.

License-included pay-as-you-go suits short-lived or no-licence cases. Azure Hybrid Benefit suits existing SA licences. Developer edition is free for non-production and Express is free for small databases on VMs.
Choose PostgreSQL or MySQL flexible server to avoid SQL Server licence cost or keep an existing open-source app. Choose Azure SQL for T-SQL and SQL Server feature dependencies.
traps: Managed Instance is not 100% compatible: FILESTREAM, FileTable, xp_cmdshell, extended stored procedures, CmdExec Agent steps and SSAS are not supported.
Azure SQL Database has no SQL Server Agent, CLR, Database Mail, Service Broker or cross-database queries. Use elastic jobs, elastic query or elastic transactions instead.
Azure Hybrid Benefit doesn't apply to the DTU model or to SQL Database serverless, and it needs Software Assurance or a qualifying subscription.
Managed Instance linked servers reach only SQL Server-family targets, not Oracle, files or Excel.
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Single Server, MySQL Single Server, Azure Database for MariaDB and Azure SQL Edge are retired, and Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is not recommended for new projects.
Native backups from Managed Instance restore only to SQL Server 2022 or 2025, depending on update policy, not to older versions.
revision: No instance features plus minimal admin: Azure SQL Database.
Instance features plus PaaS: Azure SQL Managed Instance.
OS access or unsupported features: SQL Server on Azure VMs, registered with the SQL IaaS Agent extension.
SSRS and SSAS run on a VM, although Managed Instance can host SSRS and MDS catalog databases.
PostgreSQL or MySQL app: flexible server. Large scale-out PostgreSQL: elastic clusters.
Cut licence cost with Azure Hybrid Benefit (vCore provisioned only), free Developer/Express editions, or open-source engines.
Free extended security updates for out-of-support SQL Server on Azure VMs make them the home for old versions.
